conviction_note: Counterparty and peer series published after StoneX last spoke (Marex record Jul-Sep quarter with metals revenue about 4x year on year, CME record Q3 volumes, StoneX Financial's own customer funds rising Jun $13.0bn to Jul $13.5bn to Aug $14.0bn) argue the Jul-Sep quarter did not step down from the Apr-Jun $1.00 (about $0.97 after a one-off) to the $0.86-0.91 the Street holds. That gives a fundamental beat lean of about +10%. But this name sold its last two big beats (-12.2% after a 32% EPS beat in Aug 2026, -15.5% in Aug 2025), the bar comes from two sources that disagree, and gold volatility did compress in the quarter. So p_up is only 55 on a 9-point absolute move (+0.9 scaled), against a findings sum of +1.2. The two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Diluted EPS (split-adjusted for the 3-for-2 stock dividend of 2026-07-17). Earnings Whispers consensus $0.86 (https://finviz.com/news/422592/stonex-faces-fading-volatility-test-as-street-braces-for-another-earnings-step-down, 2026-11-13). Benzinga lists $0.91 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SNEX/earnings-forecasts, undated snippet). The sweep row says one estimate is on the row, so coverage is thin. The two sources disagree by about 6%, so under the bar rule every finding is capped small. The revenue bar is unusable: $1.38bn and $276m are quoted on different revenue definitions. The company gives no quarterly guidance; its standing targets are a 15% ROE and $50m of RJO synergies, the full run rate by the end of Q1 FY27 and a mid-$40m run rate by the end of Q4 FY26. Q3 FY26 printed $1.00 against a $0.76 Zacks consensus, and Q3 included about $8.5m net of insurance recovery and a little over $4m of severance and retention.
positioning_check: Short interest: about 4.69% of float with 3.8 days to cover on the April 15 2026 settlement (MarketBeat snippet, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/SNEX/short-interest/; the page itself returned 403). Equibles shows 2.86m shares and 3.82 days on 2026-05-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/snex/short-interest). I found nothing newer, and neither figure is crowded. Skew_25d is -17.1 vol points (upside paid) with a put/call OI ratio of 0.2, but total OI is 689 and the ATM spread is 89% of mid, so the chain is too wide to mean anything. ATM IV of 86.7% at 2 DTE converts to roughly a 7.7% move, which is not usable as an anchor. Tape: the stock is -6.0% over 5 days and -4.98% over 20 days, about 15% below the post-Q3 level, under its 200-day average, and -41% from its 52-week high. Expectations are already lowered ('fading volatility' is the published preview theme).

findings.finding: Marex (MRX), StoneX's closest listed peer (non-bank FCM, metals, ag, energy), reported its Jul-Sep 2026 quarter on 2026-11-05. Revenue was a record $743.2m (+53% y/y), up $47.4m sequentially over its prior record Apr-Jun quarter. Metals revenue was $91.0m against $23.6m, on 'elevated prices and volatility' and hedging demand in precious and base metals (Levmet acquisition included). Agriculture market making was $10.8m against $0.2m. Average clearing balances were $18.7bn, +41%. StoneX's quarter covers the same three months, and the Street holds a sequential STEP DOWN for StoneX ($0.86-0.91 against $1.00).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades on the sequential trend in net operating revenue. Aug 2026: an EPS beat of $1.00 against $0.76 with NOR down 1% q/q and net income down 27% from the record Q2, and the stock fell 12.2%. May 2026: the record Q2 bought +13.6%. Aug 2025: -15.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. SNEX rose about 1.3% on 2026-11-06 (Wedbush delayed quote $54.31), then gave back about 6% over the last 5 sessions. The preview published a week later (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-13) still frames the print as 'another earnings step down' on fading volatility. If the peer read-through were priced, the stock would have re-rated toward its post-Q2 level and the consensus would have moved off $0.86. Some of Marex's growth is acquired (Winterflood, Webb, Levmet), and its gold exposure differs from StoneX's physical precious-metals book, so I sized this below the full read-through.
findings.independence: CME Group's record Q3 2026 volumes (a separate finding, https://www.cmegroup.com/media-room/press-releases/2026/10/02/cme_group_reportsrecordaveragedailyvolumeforseptemberandq3driven.html) and FIA's StoneX Financial customer-funds series (https://www.fia.org/fia/articles/august-2026-stats-customer-funds-held-us-fcms) are different sources pointing the same way.

findings.finding: CME Group reported record Q3 2026 average daily volume of 29.4m contracts, +16% y/y, and a record September of 31.8m (+22%). International ADV rose 22% to 9.0m, with international energy +40% and agricultural +28%. Exchange-traded volume and client float are the main drivers of StoneX's Institutional and Commercial (listed derivatives) lines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of the stock reacting to exchange volumes alone. The Institutional segment was +56% y/y NOR in Q3 FY26, the RJO acquisition included, and the stock fell on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry series, widely seen, and it was public six weeks before the print. The stock has fallen since, and the preview still assumes a step down. If it were transmitted to SNEX's bar, the $0.86 consensus would sit at or above Q3's $1.00. It is a proxy for StoneX's own volumes, not StoneX's own number.
findings.independence: Marex's Jul-Sep print (https://finviz.com/news/416743/marex-group-limited-announces-third-quarter-2026-results) is a separate company. Both are proxies, not StoneX's own data.

findings.finding: FIA's monthly CFTC-based tables put StoneX Financial's US customer funds at $13.0bn in June 2026, $13.5bn in July and $14.0bn in August, +7.7% from the fiscal Q3 quarter-end. It was the largest year-over-year rise among the 15 largest FCMs (+106.6%). Fed funds were unchanged through 16 Sep and then raised 25bp. Client float is the base for 'interest/fees earned on client balances', which was $111.9m of NOR in Q3 FY26, and management said it expected high-single-digit balance growth. Rising float with unchanged rates points to a flat-to-up sequential interest line rather than a decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interest and fee income on client balances recovered to $111.9m in Q3 FY26, and that recovery did not stop the -12.2% reaction. The line has not on its own driven the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: These are StoneX's own regulatory numbers, but they sit in FIA/CFTC tables that no earnings aggregator carries. If they were priced, previews would model the interest line up sequentially, yet the preview lists it only as a 'metric to watch'. The tables cover the US FCM entity only, not global client equity ($15.0bn listed-derivatives average in Q3).
findings.independence: The June and July FIA editions (https://www.fia.org/fia/articles/june-2026-stats-customer-funds-held-us-fcms) are the same series. Management's high-single-digit balance-growth comment on the Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15392596709090304) points the same way.

findings.finding: The Q3 FY26 $1.00 EPS base was flattered by about $8.5m of net insurance recovery in professional fees and partly offset by a little over $4m of severance and retention (CFO on the Q3 call). On a roughly 128m diluted share count the underlying Q3 was about $0.97, so part of the consensus step down to $0.86 is mechanical.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure is disclosed on the call, so analysts likely already strip it out of the bar. It lowers the comparison base slightly and explains about $0.03 of the $0.14 step down the Street models.
findings.independence: This finding shares the Q3 call transcript with the synergy finding below. Nothing else corroborates it.

findings.finding: Precious-metals volatility compressed in Jul-Sep 2026 against the exceptional Jan-Mar levels. StoneX's own Q4 gold outlook (2026-09-25) described gold bouncing between about $4,000 and $4,500 with volatility compressing, although silver still ranged widely (search summary of the LBMA Q3 report: $55.29 to $70.26). StoneX's physical contracts net operating revenue ($87.4m in Q3 FY26, about 12% of NOR, after all precious metals moved into Commercial) had already fallen 39% sequentially from the record Q2. A further fade in this line is the Street's 'fading volatility' thesis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (record, metals-driven) bought +13.6%. Q3 FY26, with physical revenue -39% q/q, sold -12.2%. The stock trades on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It is the published preview theme and the stock is -15% since the last print. I file it because it is the main offset to the peer read: Marex's metals strength in the same quarter was heavily base metals and copper plus an acquisition. Net of the rest of the company, about 88% of NOR is commercial ags and energy, institutional, payments and retail, and the CME, FIA and Marex data point that rest up.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers' preview (https://finviz.com/news/422592/stonex-faces-fading-volatility-test-as-street-braces-for-another-earnings-step-down) makes the same argument from the sell-side side. It contradicts the Marex finding in direction for the metals sub-line only.

findings.finding: Retail FX/CFD peers split for Jul-Sep 2026. IG Group warned on 2026-10-02 that quarterly revenue fell about 14% to £240m, on OTC revenue retention dropping to 70% from an 80% average, and cut its 2026 guide to mid-single-digit growth. Plus500 called its Q3 'excellent' on 2026-10-26 and said FY26 is tracking ahead of market expectations. StoneX's Self-Directed/Retail segment (FOREX.com, also retention-based market making) was $64.4m NOR in Q3 FY26, about 9% of the total, already -17% y/y on a 27% drop in FX/CFD ADV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The retail segment's -36% segment income in Q3 FY26 was part of the sold print.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public UK peer updates, they point in opposite directions, and they concern a small segment. The read-through to StoneX is ambiguous, so the finding is sized near zero. A UK retention dip at IG could be IG-specific (its market-making optimisation).
findings.independence: The Plus500 Q3 statement (https://www.financemagnates.com/forex/brokers/plus500-says-fy-2026-performance-tracking-above-market-forecasts/) points the other way.

findings.finding: Management guided the RJO cost-synergy run rate to the mid-$40m by the end of fiscal Q4, up from $37-38m exiting Q3, which is roughly $2m more of quarterly cost saving in Q4 and the full $50m around the end of Q1 FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Synergy progress has not visibly moved the stock (it rose from $32m to $37-38m in Q3, and the stock fell 12%).
findings.why_not_priced: This lands inside what management already guided, so it is near zero. A beat to the full $50m early would be new.
findings.independence: This finding shares the Q3 call transcript with the one-off finding. The Earnings Whispers preview repeats it.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, and the median dot for year-end 2026 rose to 4.1%. StoneX disclosed that a 100bp move in short-term rates changes annualised net income by $46.9m ($0.38 per share), partly hedged by a $2.55bn swap book at 3.51%. The hike adds roughly $0.02 a quarter to FY27 and gives management a rate tailwind to talk up on the 11-19 call. It is the closest thing to a forward guide on a name that issues none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When rates were cut in 2024-25, the stock's sensitivity to the interest line was visible in falling client-balance income. There is no clean reaction to a rate rise.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro is public, but the company-level transmission ($0.38 per 100bp) sits in the call and the 10-Q, and the forward hike path is not in the $0.86 bar for Q4 (only two weeks of it fall in the quarter). The swap book dampens it. This is macro-to-company transmission and sized small.
findings.independence: StoneX's rate sensitivity disclosure on the Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15392596709090304).

findings.finding: Net bad-debt expense rose to $12.6m for the first nine months of FY26 from $2.3m a year earlier (Zacks, citing the Q3 10-Q; snippet only, page blocked). Zacks flagged it as a credit watch item, and a fiscal year-end could carry further provisions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Zacks tied the post-Q3 drop partly to credit concerns. Allinvestview attributed it to the sequential deceleration.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-30; the figure is from a Zacks snippet citing it, snippet_only)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it was public in August and flagged by Zacks. I file it as a tail risk because a single large client default is the classic FCM miss. Short interest is not crowded (about 4.7% of float, 3.8 days to cover), so there is no squeeze offset.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-02 StoneX agreed to acquire Integra Trading S.A.S., a Colombian coffee exporter and processor, for its Swiss physical trading arm, described as 'immediately accretive'. It also launched OTC cotton derivatives with Cotlook and a Singapore FX booking centre on 2026-10-01. These are small bolt-ons and do not affect the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Small acquisitions have not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public and small, and are probably priced. I file them for completeness.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive. That agrees with the (unusable) upside-paid skew and cuts against the negative run-up, but the tape (-15% since the last print, -6% over 5 days) already reflects the 'fading volatility' consensus the findings argue against. The bigger tension is the name's own reaction function, which has sold large beats.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, bar from two sources that disagree ($0.86 EW against $0.91 Benzinga, one estimate on the row): capped the beat-dependent findings. Marex 1.5 to 1.0, CME 0.8 to 0.5, FIA 1.0 to 0.7.
Rule 1, a verified fact is not a predicted reaction: this name sold a 32% EPS beat for -12.2% and fell -15.5% in Aug 2025. p_up 58 to 55, scaled move 1.44 to 0.9.
Rule 9, segment net of the rest: the metals fade is sized against about 12% of NOR while the rest of the company's proxies point up. -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 5 and Rule 7: the Fed transmission is kept small as a proxy (0.5 to 0.4). The bad-debt negative is left at -0.5 after checking short interest (not crowded).
Left unchanged: abs_move_pct at 9.0. Thin coverage argues up, the disputed bar does not argue down.
